extracted.intended_audience: AAPI journalists, journalism students, media professionals, allies, and prospective AAJA members
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Asian American Journalists Association's mission, history, strategic priorities, and programmatic approaches to increasing AAPI representation, ensuring accurate coverage, and supporting members and students in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase AAPI perspectives and representation in newsrooms, media, and storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: The heart of AAJA’s four-fold mission is to increase AAPI perspectives and representation in newsrooms, media, and storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAJA pursues this goal via trainings, opportunities, resources, and by nurturing a network and community of AAPI journalists globally; it also emphasizes leadership development to put AAPIs into newsroom management and executive roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide encouragement, information, advice, and scholarship assistance to AAPI students
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide encouragement, information, advice and scholarship assistance to AAPI students who aspire to professional journalism careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly one-third of AAJA’s members are students, and AAJA runs career development and mentorship programs that prioritize diversity and bring young people into the news business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide the AAPI community awareness of news media and how to gain fair access
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide to the AAPI community an awareness of news media and an understanding of how to gain fair access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAJA supports work that trains local and community organizations to engage with the media (e.g., Media Access) so communities understand and can seek fair coverage and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide means of association and support among AAPI journalists and advance them into management
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a means of association and support among Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) journalists, and to advance AAPI journalists as news managers and media executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAJA builds chapters and a membership network (U.S. and Asia) to foster peer support, mentorship, and pathways into leadership positions in news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and call out inaccuracies and unfair coverage of AAPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: To research and point out when news media organizations stray from accuracy and fairness in the coverage of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders and AAPI issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAJA conducts MediaWatch activities and produces content (AAJA Studio) to identify problematic coverage and hold newsrooms accountable for accuracy and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Champion development of AAPI representation and leadership through trainings, opportunities, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to champion the development of AAPI representation and leadership in journalism through trainings, opportunities, and resources for members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic priorities include evolving career-development and mentorship programs that adapt as journalism changes; coordination and synthesis of programs is emphasized to strengthen impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen civic engagement and accountability efforts (MediaWatch, AAJA Studio, Media Access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen AAJA’s civic engagement arm which holds newsrooms accountable to accurate reporting on AAPIs and trains local/community organizations to engage with the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific initiatives named include MediaWatch and AAJA Studio for newsroom accountability and Media Access for training communities on media engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize addressing the 'pipeline' problem for AAPI journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and act on the persistent 'pipeline' problem that limits the number of AAPI journalists reaching senior-level roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAJA sees coordinated programmatic work, mentorship, scholarships, and attention to economic disruptions (e.g., recession, COVID-19 impacts) as necessary to preserve and strengthen the pipeline into leadership.
